intended_object: Given a pairing (bicharacter) e : X × Y → 𝕋 of commutative groups and a subgroup V ≤ Y, the left annihilator (orthogonal) V^⊥ = {x ∈ X | e(x, y) = 1 for all y ∈ V}, a subgroup of X. This comes from the docstring and the name.
explanation:
The definition is faithful. `rightCharacter e` is the flipped pairing Y →* (X →* Circle), defined by y ↦ (x ↦ e x y). `rightAnnihilator U f` is {y | ∀ x ∈ U, f x y = 1}. Putting these together, `leftAnnihilator V e` has carrier {x | ∀ y ∈ V, e x y = 1}, which is exactly the left annihilator. Degenerate cases also come out right: if V = ⊥, the result is all of X.

The codomain is the circle group, which is the standard setting for Pontryagin-style duality of restricted products, so this is the natural setting for the library. The construction itself would work for any target commutative group. I found no Mathlib definition of annihilators for group bicharacters, so there is no general Mathlib notion this duplicates.
